subject: maths-literacy
notes: v2.0 condensed from v1.0 (135 → 85 atomic skills) for cleaner skill-tree UX. L4 (13 skills) kept identical because L4 question banks reference these IDs. L4 prereq pointers remapped to the condensed L1/L2/L3 IDs.

levels.title: Numbers, calculations and estimation
levels.description: Foundation number skills used in every Application Topic: formats, operations, estimation, rounding, ratio, proportion, rates, percentages.

atomic_skills.title: Read and use numbers in different formats and conventions
atomic_skills.description: Work with decimal comma and point, thousands separators (space and comma), word formats up to billions, signed values (debit/credit, temperature), and non-numerical number conventions in context (cricket overs, building numbering, time).

error_signatures.description: Treats decimal comma and point as different numbers
error_signatures.example: Reads 1,2 as 12 instead of 1.2

error_signatures.description: Performs arithmetic on a coded number as if it were a quantity
error_signatures.example: Adds two flat numbers like 1214 + 305 to find total floors

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Show the same value in two formats side by side. For coded numbers, ask the learner to describe what each digit represents before any arithmetic.

atomic_skills.title: Add, subtract, multiply and divide; powers of 10
atomic_skills.description: Perform all four operations on whole numbers and decimals (with and without calculator). Multiply and divide by 10, 100, 1 000 mentally for unit conversions.

error_signatures.description: Misplaces decimal point in product or quotient
error_signatures.example: 1,5 × 0,2 calculated as 0,03 or 3,0

error_signatures.description: Shifts the decimal point the wrong direction for ×÷10/100/1000
error_signatures.example: Calculates 45,3 ÷ 100 as 4530 instead of 0,453

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Estimate first as a sanity check. For decimals, count decimal places in factors. For powers of 10, anchor with money (R1,50 × 100 = R150).

atomic_skills.title: BODMAS, brackets, squares, roots and fractions
atomic_skills.description: Apply order of operations (BODMAS). Use brackets correctly in formula substitution. Calculate squares, cubes, square roots with a basic calculator. Add, subtract, multiply, divide fractions; convert between fractions, decimals and percentages.

error_signatures.description: Evaluates left-to-right ignoring BODMAS
error_signatures.example: Computes 5 + 2 × 3 as 21 instead of 11

error_signatures.description: Adds fractions by adding numerators and denominators separately

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: BODMAS: underline operations in priority order before computing. For fraction addition, force a common denominator first.

atomic_skills.title: Estimate, round and sense-check in context
atomic_skills.description: Estimate before calculating as a sanity check. Round off / up / down / to nearest 5, choosing the right rounding for context (money to 2dp, paint litres up, people whole, supermarket totals to 5c).

error_signatures.description: Rounds in wrong direction for the context
error_signatures.example: Calculates 6,2 litres of paint and buys 6 litres instead of rounding up to next-available pack size

error_signatures.description: Accepts a calculator answer that is orders of magnitude wrong
error_signatures.example: Accepts 101,098 for 198 × 5,1 (off by a factor of 10)

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Estimate by rounding each input to one significant figure first. For rounding direction, ask: what is being counted, and do you need at least the calculated amount or are you limited by what you have?

atomic_skills.title: Work with ratios and direct proportion
atomic_skills.description: Convert between forms of a ratio (a:b, a/b, unit form). Find missing terms; divide a quantity in a given ratio. Apply direct proportion (price per unit, scaling quantities).

error_signatures.description: Treats parts of a ratio as fractions of one whole
error_signatures.example: For ratio 1:2:2 with 50 wheelbarrows cement, gives 50/5 = 10 sand instead of 100

error_signatures.description: Uses wrong operation when scaling
error_signatures.example: Given 50 m² costs R1 750, multiplies instead of dividing for 1 m² cost

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Add ratio parts to find total shares, then divide. For direct proportion, find the unit value first, then scale.

atomic_skills.title: Inverse (indirect) proportion in context
atomic_skills.description: When one quantity increases, the other decreases proportionally — product stays constant (e.g. teachers in a taxi scheme × cost per teacher = fixed monthly hire).

error_signatures.description: Treats inverse proportion as direct
error_signatures.example: Says cost per teacher doubles when teachers double, instead of halves

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Ask: as one increases, does the other go up or down? If down, it's inverse — use total ÷ number.

atomic_skills.title: Calculate and compare rates
atomic_skills.description: Cost rates (R/kg), consumption rates (L/100km), speed rates (km/h). Simplify to unit form to compare which is cheaper / faster / more efficient.

error_signatures.description: Compares rates without converting to the same unit
error_signatures.example: Compares R42,99/4kg with R47,50/5kg by total instead of per-kg cost

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Always divide to get the per-unit value before comparing.

atomic_skills.title: Calculate percentages and percentage of value
atomic_skills.description: Find % of value (14% discount on R200). Increase a value by a % (5% price rise). Decrease a value by a % (10% sale). Includes VAT calculations.

error_signatures.description: Forgets to add or subtract the % amount from the original
error_signatures.example: After a 5% increase on R8,20, gives R0,41 instead of R8,61

error_signatures.description: Confuses 'percentage of' with 'percent off'
error_signatures.example: Treats '15% off R200' as R30 final price

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Two-step it: calculate the % amount, then add or subtract. Or use multiplier shortcut: ×1,05 for +5%, ×0,90 for -10%.

atomic_skills.title: Percentage change and reverse percentages
atomic_skills.description: Calculate % change between two values: (new − old) ÷ old × 100. Find the original value when given a value after a % change (reverse %).

error_signatures.description: Divides change by new value instead of old
error_signatures.example: Computes (52,49 − 48,99) / 52,49 for the % rise

error_signatures.description: Applies % to the new value when reversing
error_signatures.example: Adds 15% of R325 to R325 to find original, instead of dividing R325 by 0,85

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Anchor: percentage change is calculated against the STARTING value. For reverse %, set up new = original × (1 ± %) and solve.

levels.title: Patterns, relationships and representations
levels.description: Read and interpret graphs, identify the type of relationship between variables, move between tables / equations / graphs, and compare two or more relationships (Gr 11+12).

atomic_skills.title: Read story-graphs and identify variables
atomic_skills.description: Describe in plain language what a graph shows. Identify dependent vs independent variables; distinguish discrete (counts) from continuous (measured) data.

error_signatures.description: Describes shape without linking to variables
error_signatures.example: Says 'the line goes up' without naming what is increasing

error_signatures.description: Reverses dependency
error_signatures.example: Says talktime depends on cost

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Force a sentence: 'As [x variable] increases, [y variable] [increases / decreases / stays the same].' Independent goes on horizontal axis.

atomic_skills.title: Read critical points and paired values from graphs
atomic_skills.description: Find where a graph crosses axes, reaches max / min, or intersects another graph. Read off dependent value for given independent value (and vice versa).

error_signatures.description: Reads wrong axis at the critical point
error_signatures.example: At max, reports x-coordinate as the max value

error_signatures.description: Reads values misaligned with grid lines
error_signatures.example: Reads x = 30 when point is at x = 35

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Trace down to x-axis AND across to y-axis; write both coordinates before deciding which answers the question. Use a ruler; check the scale.

atomic_skills.title: Identify constant and linear (constant-difference) relationships
atomic_skills.description: Constant: y stays the same (fixed monthly subscription). Linear: y increases by a constant amount per unit increase in x (R7,50 per litre).

error_signatures.description: Confuses a fixed-then-linear relationship with purely linear
error_signatures.example: Treats cell contract with 100 free minutes then R1,50/min as linear from 0

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Calculate difference between consecutive table values. Zero = constant. Same non-zero = linear. Changes mid-table = piecewise.

atomic_skills.title: Identify inverse proportion relationships
atomic_skills.description: When y × x = constant: as x grows, y shrinks. Used in shared-cost scenarios.

error_signatures.description: Confuses inverse curve with a decreasing straight line
error_signatures.example: Draws inverse proportion as a straight line sloping down

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Check: does y × x stay the same for every pair? If yes, inverse. Graph is a curve approaching but never touching both axes.

atomic_skills.title: Identify constant-ratio (compound growth) relationships
atomic_skills.description: Each term = previous term × fixed factor (compound interest: balance grows by 0,5% of previous month's balance). Grade 11+12 only.

error_signatures.description: Treats compound growth as linear
error_signatures.example: Calculates 5% on original principal each period instead of running balance

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Check ratio between consecutive values. If new ÷ previous is constant, it's compound. Each period uses the new balance as the next base.

tiers.title: Tables, equations and graphs as representations

atomic_skills.title: Move between tables, equations and graphs
atomic_skills.description: The same relationship can be shown three ways. Fill a table from an equation, plot a graph from a table, write an equation from a table. Substitute values; solve by trial-and-improvement. Plot graphs with appropriate scale, axes, labels.

error_signatures.description: Plots points with x-value as y-coordinate
Substitutes value for the wrong variable
error_signatures.example: In cost = 1,50m + 100, substitutes 250 for m when 250 is cost

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Write coordinates as (independent, dependent). Read the equation out loud naming each variable. Always label axes with variable name AND unit.

atomic_skills.title: Identify intersection and compare options
atomic_skills.description: When two graphs cross, dependent value is the same for both. Use crossover to recommend best option for a given range, and justify with rates of change. Grade 11+12 only (Gr 12 = 2 or more relationships).

error_signatures.description: States intersection without interpreting
error_signatures.example: Answers 'at x = 200' without explaining what it means

error_signatures.description: Picks one option without noting it depends on range
error_signatures.example: Says 'Contract A always cheaper' ignoring 200-min crossover

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Finish with: 'At [crossover], [both options] give the same [dependent]. Below that, [A] wins; above that, [B].' Break range into intervals.

levels.title: Finance: documents, income and budgets
levels.caps_section: Finance — Financial documents; Income, expenditure, profit/loss; Budgets; Cost price and selling price
levels.description: Read household financial documents. Compile income-and-expenditure statements and budgets. Determine cost and selling price.

atomic_skills.title: Read household bills, till slips and bank statements
atomic_skills.description: Identify account holders, periods, consumption, charges, VAT, debits/credits, running balance. Verify totals from line items. Distinguish VAT-inclusive vs VAT-exclusive amounts.

error_signatures.description: Adds VAT to an amount that already includes VAT
error_signatures.example: Multiplies VAT-inclusive amount by 1,15 again

error_signatures.description: Treats a debit as adding to balance
error_signatures.example: Adds a -R450 grocery debit instead of subtracting

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Always check VAT inclusion before calculating. Anchor: debit = money out; credit = money in. Verify quoted total by summing line items.

atomic_skills.title: Read a payslip
atomic_skills.description: Identify gross pay, deductions (PAYE, UIF, medical aid, pension), taxable income, net pay. Verify net pay = gross − total deductions.

error_signatures.description: Confuses gross and net pay
error_signatures.example: Treats net pay as the salary used for tax calculations

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Anchor: gross = before deductions; net = take-home. Tax is calculated on taxable income (gross minus certain pre-tax deductions).

atomic_skills.title: Calculate income, expenditure and profit/loss
atomic_skills.description: Sum income sources and expenses for a household or business over a period. Profit = income − expenditure; report as profit (positive) or loss (negative magnitude).

error_signatures.description: Mixes income and expense items into a single total
error_signatures.example: Adds salary and rent into 'monthly cash flow'

error_signatures.description: Reports a negative profit instead of naming it as a loss
error_signatures.example: Says 'profit = -R500' rather than 'loss of R500'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Separate items into two columns (income vs expenditure) before summing. If expenditure exceeds income, name it a loss.

atomic_skills.title: Construct an income-and-expenditure statement
atomic_skills.description: Arrange income items, expense items and resulting profit/loss into a structured statement for a household or small business.

error_signatures.description: Includes once-off lump sums in a monthly statement without prorating
error_signatures.example: Adds R12 000 annual school fees as a single monthly expense

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: List every item with its frequency. Convert all to the same period (monthly) before tabulating.

atomic_skills.title: Classify expenses and construct a budget
atomic_skills.description: Classify expenses as fixed (same each period), variable (changes with use), or unexpected (one-off). Estimate income and expenses for a future period; allocate amounts; check planned expenses do not exceed expected income.

error_signatures.description: Treats all monthly bills as fixed regardless of consumption
error_signatures.example: Classifies electricity as fixed because it is billed monthly

error_signatures.description: Omits recurring expense or plans no savings/contingency
error_signatures.example: Allocates 100% of income to known expenses, leaving no buffer

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Ask: would the amount be the same next month if usage changes? Use a checklist of common categories before finalising.

atomic_skills.title: Compare actual vs budgeted values; identify variance
atomic_skills.description: Compare budgeted against actual. Calculate variance (actual − budget) and percentage variance. Identify over- and under-spend categories.

error_signatures.description: Treats every overspend as bad without context
error_signatures.example: Flags a R100 overspend due to a guest as a budgeting failure

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Quantify variance in both Rand and percentage. Comment on which matter (>10% or large absolute) vs noise.

atomic_skills.title: Calculate cost price and selling price using markup
atomic_skills.description: Cost price = sum of component costs (materials + labour + overhead per item). Selling price = cost × (1 + markup %). Also calculate markup % given cost and selling price; distinguish markup from profit margin.

error_signatures.description: Omits a component cost (labour or packaging)
error_signatures.example: Calculates cake cost from ingredients only, ignoring electricity and packaging

error_signatures.description: Confuses markup with profit margin
error_signatures.example: Treats 'mark up 25%' as 'profit margin 25% of selling price'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: List every input that goes into one unit before adding. Markup is on cost price; margin is on selling price.

atomic_skills.title: Calculate income from sales
atomic_skills.description: Income = selling price × volume sold. Project income for different sales volumes. Distinguish income from profit.

error_signatures.description: Confuses income with profit
error_signatures.example: Subtracts cost from income but reports the income value as the answer

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Income = total money in. Profit = income − total costs. Use both labels explicitly.

levels.title: Finance: tariffs, interest and break-even
levels.caps_section: Finance — Tariff systems; Break-even analysis; Interest (simple and compound)
levels.description: Compare tariff structures (electricity, water, cell phone). Find break-even points. Calculate simple and compound interest. Model loan and investment scenarios.

atomic_skills.title: Read a tariff structure
atomic_skills.description: Interpret a tariff table or formula: fixed charge, per-unit rate, block tariffs (different rate at different usage levels), VAT inclusion.

error_signatures.description: Reads a stepped tariff as flat
error_signatures.example: Multiplies total kWh by the first-block rate without recognising the higher rate above the threshold

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Highlight each block boundary and the rate that applies in each block before any calculation.

atomic_skills.title: Calculate cost from a tariff and consumption
atomic_skills.description: Given a tariff and a consumption value, compute the total charge. Includes block tariffs (compute per-block then sum) and add-on fees.

error_signatures.description: Applies the highest block rate to all consumption rather than only the portion above the threshold
error_signatures.example: For 700 kWh on a 0-500 kWh @ R2 / 500+ @ R3 tariff, computes 700 × R3 instead of 500 × R2 + 200 × R3

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Split consumption into pieces that fit each block. Charge each piece at the block rate. Sum the pieces.

atomic_skills.title: Compare two tariff systems
atomic_skills.description: Build cost tables for two tariffs across a range of consumption. Identify which is cheaper at each usage level and explain the crossover.

error_signatures.description: Declares one tariff better without specifying usage range
error_signatures.example: Says 'Tariff A is cheaper' without noting it only holds below 200 kWh

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Always identify the crossover point. Below it, one tariff wins; above it, the other. State both ranges.

atomic_skills.title: Define break-even in context
atomic_skills.description: Break-even = the point where total income equals total cost; profit = zero. Explain what 'break-even' means for a given business or scenario.

error_signatures.description: Confuses break-even with the start of profit
error_signatures.example: Defines break-even as 'when you start making money' rather than the exact point where income = cost

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Anchor: at break-even, profit is zero. One more sale = first rand of profit. One less sale = first rand of loss.

atomic_skills.title: Find break-even from a table of values
atomic_skills.description: Given a table showing income and expenditure across different quantities (or time), identify the row where they are closest or equal.

error_signatures.description: Reports the first profitable row instead of the break-even row
error_signatures.example: Reports n = 51 as break-even when the table shows income = cost exactly at n = 50

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Look for the row where income − cost = 0, or where the sign of the difference flips.

atomic_skills.title: Find break-even from the intersection of two graphs
atomic_skills.description: Plot income and cost graphs on the same axes. Identify the point of intersection as break-even. Interpret regions on either side as profit / loss zones.

error_signatures.description: Identifies intersection but cannot label the regions
error_signatures.example: Names the break-even point but cannot say whether the region to the right is profit or loss

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: After finding the intersection, pick one point to the left and one to the right. Compare income to cost at each. Label the regions accordingly.

atomic_skills.title: Interpret profit and loss zones from a cost/revenue graph
atomic_skills.description: Explain in plain language what the graph shows: minimum sales for survival, expected profit at planned volume, sensitivity to cost increases.

error_signatures.description: Reports values without business interpretation
error_signatures.example: Says 'break-even is at 50 units' without explaining why this matters for the owner

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Translate every number into a decision: 'The owner must sell at least 50 cakes to cover costs. Selling 60 yields R200 profit.'

atomic_skills.title: Calculate simple interest
atomic_skills.description: Use A = P(1 + i × n). Identify principal (P), interest rate per period (i), number of periods (n). Compute interest earned or owed and total amount.

error_signatures.description: Uses interest rate as percentage instead of decimal
error_signatures.example: Substitutes i = 8 instead of i = 0,08 for 8% per annum

error_signatures.description: Mismatches rate period and time period
error_signatures.example: Uses annual rate with months without converting

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Always convert % to decimal. Always check rate period matches time period (annual rate with years, monthly rate with months).

atomic_skills.title: Calculate total amount after simple interest
atomic_skills.description: Total amount A = P + interest = P(1 + in). Distinguish interest amount from total amount.

error_signatures.description: Reports interest amount when asked for total amount (or vice versa)
error_signatures.example: When asked for 'final balance', gives the R interest figure not the principal + interest

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Read the question twice: are you asked for interest earned or total at end? Write the answer with a label.

atomic_skills.title: Calculate compound interest manually period by period
atomic_skills.description: Compute interest on the new (growing) balance each period, not the original principal. Build a table showing opening balance, interest, closing balance.

error_signatures.description: Applies interest to original principal each period (treats as simple)
error_signatures.example: Computes year 3 interest as P × i instead of (year 2 closing balance) × i

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Build a 3-column table: opening balance, interest = opening × i, closing balance = opening + interest. The closing balance becomes next period's opening.

atomic_skills.title: Compare simple vs compound interest over the same period
atomic_skills.description: Calculate both on the same principal, rate, and time. Show in a table or graph how compound exceeds simple over multiple periods.

error_signatures.description: Concludes they are equal because year 1 values match
error_signatures.example: Says simple = compound after seeing identical year 1 interest figures

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Always extend the comparison to at least 3 periods. The gap widens with each period.

atomic_skills.title: Model a loan or investment scenario
atomic_skills.description: Build a multi-row table showing month/year, opening balance, interest, repayment (loan) or contribution (investment), closing balance.

error_signatures.description: Applies the repayment before the interest
error_signatures.example: Reduces balance by repayment first, then computes interest on the reduced amount

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Order each row: opening → add interest → subtract repayment (or add contribution) → closing.

atomic_skills.title: Investigate impact of rate changes or extra repayments
atomic_skills.description: Re-run the loan/investment model with a changed interest rate or a higher monthly repayment. Compare total interest paid or final balance.

error_signatures.description: Compares only the monthly figures, not total cost
error_signatures.example: Reports that higher repayment 'costs more per month' without noting it shortens the loan and reduces total interest

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Always report two numbers: months to repay AND total interest paid over the loan life. Decisions depend on both.

levels.title: Finance: banking, taxation, inflation, exchange rates
levels.caps_section: Finance — Banking, loans and investments; Taxation; Inflation; Exchange rates
levels.description: Read bank statements and fee schedules, compare accounts, calculate PAYE and UIF, work with tax brackets and rebates, calculate inflation, perform currency conversions.

atomic_skills.title: Read bank statements and calculate fees
atomic_skills.description: Distinguish account types. Identify debits, credits, fees, balances. Use a bank fee schedule (per-transaction, per-withdrawal, monthly) to calculate total charges.

error_signatures.description: Counts the same transaction twice when applying fees
error_signatures.example: Counts an ATM withdrawal as both withdrawal and balance enquiry

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Mark opening and closing balance lines first. For fees, categorise each transaction before counting and multiplying by per-category fee.

atomic_skills.title: Compare bank accounts and loan options
atomic_skills.description: Given two or more account fee structures and a transaction profile, calculate total monthly cost on each and recommend the cheaper. For loans, use a model to determine monthly repayment, total amount paid, and total interest.

error_signatures.description: Recommends without tying it to the user's transaction profile
error_signatures.example: Says 'Account A is cheaper' without noting it only holds for heavy users

error_signatures.description: Reports monthly loan cost while ignoring total cost of credit
error_signatures.example: Says 'R450/month is affordable' without computing R450 × 60 = R27 000 on a R20 000 loan

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Always tie recommendations to the user's profile. For loans, compute total paid AND total interest, not just monthly.

atomic_skills.title: Identify taxable income and use a tax deduction table
atomic_skills.description: Read a payslip to distinguish gross pay, pre-tax deductions, taxable income, PAYE, UIF, net pay. Use a SARS tax deduction table to find the monthly PAYE for a given taxable income.

error_signatures.description: Treats gross pay as the basis for PAYE
error_signatures.example: Computes PAYE on R30 000 gross instead of R28 500 taxable income after pension deduction

error_signatures.description: Reads the wrong row of the deduction table
error_signatures.example: For R28 500 income, reads off the R29 000 row by mistake

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Taxable income = gross − pre-tax deductions. Use a ruler to align the income value with the PAYE column.

atomic_skills.title: Calculate PAYE from a tax bracket formula
atomic_skills.description: Use SARS tax bracket tables: identify the bracket the annual income falls in, apply 'base + rate × (income − threshold)' to compute annual tax.

error_signatures.description: Applies the rate to total income rather than excess above threshold
error_signatures.example: For R414 000 income in '226 001-353 100 + 26% above 226 000' bracket, computes 26% × R414 000 instead of 26% × (414 000 − 226 000)

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Rewrite the formula filling in threshold and income: tax = base + rate × (income − threshold). Compute the bracketed expression first.

atomic_skills.title: Annualise income, apply rebates and calculate UIF
atomic_skills.description: Convert monthly salary to annual for bracket lookup (and back). Subtract age-band rebate from annual tax. Calculate UIF (1% of gross capped at SARS-set ceiling).

error_signatures.description: Forgets to subtract the primary rebate
error_signatures.example: Reports R94 320 annual tax instead of R94 320 − R17 235 = R77 085 after rebate

error_signatures.description: Forgets the UIF earnings cap
error_signatures.example: Calculates UIF as 1% of R30 000 gross when capped at lower ceiling

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Sequence: monthly × 12 = annual income → bracket formula → subtract rebate → ÷ 12 for monthly PAYE. For UIF, check the cap before applying 1%.

atomic_skills.title: Calculate the effect of inflation over single and multiple periods
atomic_skills.description: Single period: new = old × (1 + i). Multiple periods (compound inflation): new = old × (1 + i)^n. Recognise inflation as compound growth.

error_signatures.description: Reports the increase amount instead of the new price
error_signatures.example: For R100 with 6% inflation, gives R6 instead of R106

error_signatures.description: Multiplies the single-year increase by n instead of compounding
error_signatures.example: For 5 years at 6%, computes new = old × (1 + 0,06 × 5) instead of × 1,06^5

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use the multiplier (1 + i) once per period. For multi-year, raise to the power of n (or table it year by year).

atomic_skills.title: Explain inflation's effect on buying power and salaries
atomic_skills.description: Argue with calculations: a 5% salary increase in a 6% inflation year is a real-terms decrease. Justify a salary increase request using inflation data.

error_signatures.description: Treats any pay rise as a real gain
error_signatures.example: Says '5% raise = better off' without comparing to inflation

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Frame: 'A raise is a real gain only if it exceeds inflation. Otherwise buying power has fallen.'

atomic_skills.title: Convert between currencies and account for fees
atomic_skills.description: Given a rate (1 USD = R18,50), convert between currencies in either direction. Account for bank commission (% of amount + flat fee).

error_signatures.description: Multiplies when should divide (or vice versa)
error_signatures.example: To convert R3 700 to USD at R18,50/USD, multiplies instead of dividing

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Write the rate as a sentence: '1 USD = R18,50'. To go FROM R TO USD, divide. FROM USD TO R, multiply. Net fees before/after conversion consistently.

atomic_skills.title: Compare prices across countries (e.g. Big Mac Index)
atomic_skills.description: Convert prices to a common currency. Discuss what the difference says about purchasing power and exchange rate fairness, paired with local wages.

error_signatures.description: Concludes 'cheaper country is better' without considering local wages
error_signatures.example: Says 'a Big Mac is cheaper in SA, so SA is cheaper to live in' without comparing average wage

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Pair every price comparison with a wage or cost-of-living comparison before drawing affordability conclusions.

levels.title: Measurement: length, time, conversions
levels.caps_section: Measurement — Conversions; Measuring length, weight, volume, temperature; Time
levels.description: Foundation measurement: metric conversions, reading instruments, time formats and calculations, temperature.

atomic_skills.title: Convert metric units (length, mass, volume)
atomic_skills.description: Convert between mm/cm/m/km, g/kg/tonnes, ml/L/kL/m³ using powers of 10. Apply 1 m³ = 1 000 L for water tanks, pools, fuel.

error_signatures.description: Wrong conversion factor (×10 vs ×100 vs ×1000)
error_signatures.example: Converts 2,5 km to m as 250 instead of 2 500

error_signatures.description: Treats m³ as equivalent to m for purposes of conversion
error_signatures.example: Converts 5 m³ to litres as 5 000 (treating as 5 m of length)

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Memorise: 10mm=1cm, 100cm=1m, 1000m=1km; 1kg=1000g; 1m³=1000L. Going smaller unit, multiply. Going larger, divide.

atomic_skills.title: Convert temperature (°C to °F)
atomic_skills.description: Apply the conversion formula F = 1,8 × C + 32 (or the reverse). Used for weather, baking from foreign sources.

error_signatures.description: Adds 32 before multiplying by 1,8
error_signatures.example: For 20°C, computes (20+32) × 1,8 = 93,6°F instead of 1,8 × 20 + 32 = 68°F

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: BODMAS: ×1,8 first, then +32.

atomic_skills.title: Measure accurately and apply measured lengths
atomic_skills.description: Read measurements to the nearest mm, account for zero offset, use appropriate instrument. Apply measured lengths to real-world tasks (carpeting, fencing, fitting objects).

error_signatures.description: Starts measuring from end of ruler rather than zero mark
error_signatures.example: Reads a 5 cm rod as 5,5 cm because ruler zero is offset from edge

error_signatures.description: Adds same dimension twice when calculating perimeter
error_signatures.example: For 4m × 3m room, computes perimeter as 4 + 3 = 7m

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Align zero mark (not the edge) with one end. Sketch shapes and label every side before adding.

atomic_skills.title: Read time formats and calculate intervals
atomic_skills.description: Convert 12-hour and 24-hour formats (14:30 ↔ 2:30 pm). Recognise 00:00 as midnight, 12:00 as noon. Calculate elapsed time, durations across midnight.

error_signatures.description: Treats 12:00 as midnight instead of noon
error_signatures.example: Says 12:30 lunch is at half past midnight

error_signatures.description: Subtracts hours and minutes as decimals
error_signatures.example: Computes 10:15 − 9:45 as 0,70 hours instead of 30 minutes

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Anchor: 12:00 = noon, 00:00 = midnight. For subtraction, do minutes first (borrowing 60 if needed), then hours.

atomic_skills.title: Read and interpret timetables
atomic_skills.description: Use bus, train, flight timetables to find departure / arrival times, journey durations, connection times.

error_signatures.description: Misreads row vs column on a timetable grid
error_signatures.example: Reports a stop's arrival time as the column header time

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use finger or ruler to follow row and column. Verify cell value matches the question.

atomic_skills.title: Plan trips using time, distance and speed
atomic_skills.description: Use distance ÷ speed = time. Plan a journey including stops, refuelling. Account for time zones in international travel.

error_signatures.description: Ignores rest stops and breaks in journey planning
error_signatures.example: Plans a 14-hour drive with no rest breaks

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Add a buffer for stops. Total planned time = driving time + breaks.

atomic_skills.title: Read and interpret temperature
atomic_skills.description: Read thermometers (analog and digital). Interpret weather forecasts. Decide actions based on temperature (e.g. medical concerns above 38°C).

error_signatures.description: Reads sub-zero temperatures as positive
error_signatures.example: Reads -3°C as 3°C, missing the negative

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Always check for the negative sign on a thermometer reading. Below zero on a scale means below freezing.

levels.title: Measurement: perimeter, area, volume, mass
levels.caps_section: Measurement — Perimeter, area and volume; Mass / weight (dosage)
levels.description: Calculate perimeter, area, surface area, volume of basic and composite shapes. Apply to real-world tasks: paint, tiling, concrete, water tanks, packaging, dosage.

atomic_skills.title: Calculate dosage and convert to medicine units
atomic_skills.description: Apply per-kg dosage rule to body weight to find safe dose (mg). Convert dose in mg to volume or count given concentration (e.g. 120 mg per 5 ml syrup, mg per tablet).

error_signatures.description: Confuses dose-per-kg with total dose
error_signatures.example: For 25 kg child and 10 mg/kg rule, gives 10 mg instead of 250 mg

error_signatures.description: Inverts the concentration ratio
error_signatures.example: For 250 mg dose at 120 mg/5ml, gives 250 × 120 ÷ 5 instead of 250 × 5 ÷ 120

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: weight (kg) × rate (mg/kg) = total dose. Set up volume conversion as proportion: (dose ÷ concentration) × volume per dose.

atomic_skills.title: Interpret weight charts and BMI
atomic_skills.description: Read percentile growth charts. Calculate BMI = mass (kg) ÷ height² (m²) and interpret against standard categories.

error_signatures.description: Uses height in cm rather than m in BMI
error_signatures.example: For 1,7 m tall, divides by 170² instead of 1,7²

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: BMI formula needs height in METRES. Convert cm to m before squaring.

atomic_skills.title: Calculate perimeter of basic and composite shapes
atomic_skills.description: Rectangle: 2(l+b). Triangle: a+b+c. Circle (circumference): π × d. Composite: sum all outer sides; deduce unmarked sides from marked ones.

error_signatures.description: Confuses perimeter formula with area formula
error_signatures.example: Computes rectangle perimeter as l × b

error_signatures.description: Misses an interior side of an L-shape
error_signatures.example: For L-shape with 6 outer sides, sums only 4

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Perimeter = total length around the shape. Walk the perimeter with your finger and count every side.

atomic_skills.title: Calculate area of basic and composite shapes
atomic_skills.description: Rectangle: l × b. Triangle: ½ × base × perpendicular height. Circle: πr² (r from d ÷ 2). Composite: break into rectangles/triangles/semicircles; add or subtract for cut-outs.

error_signatures.description: Uses slanted side instead of perpendicular height for triangle
error_signatures.example: For triangle base 6 cm hypotenuse 5 cm perpendicular height 4 cm, computes ½ × 6 × 5

error_signatures.description: Adds cut-out instead of subtracting
error_signatures.example: For square with circular hole, sums square + circle areas instead of subtracting circle

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Triangle area uses perpendicular height (90° to base). For composites, mark each region 'add' or 'subtract' before calculating.

atomic_skills.title: Apply area to real-world tasks (paint, tiles, garden)
atomic_skills.description: Use area calculations with a conversion ratio (e.g. 1 L paint covers 8 m²) to determine quantity to buy. Round up to next available pack size.

error_signatures.description: Reports exact litres without rounding up to available pack size
error_signatures.example: Reports needing 13,75 L paint without going to 4 × 5L = 20L

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Two rounding steps: round litres up to whole, then up to next-available pack size.

atomic_skills.title: Calculate volume of basic 3D shapes
atomic_skills.description: Rectangular prism: l × b × h. Cylinder: π × r² × h. Apply to boxes, rooms, water tanks, cans, pipes. Convert to capacity via 1 m³ = 1 000 L.

error_signatures.description: Multiplies only two of three dimensions of a prism
error_signatures.example: For 2m × 1,5m × 1m tank, computes 2 × 1,5 = 3 m² instead of 3 m³

error_signatures.description: Forgets to square the radius for a cylinder
error_signatures.example: Computes π × r × h instead of π × r² × h

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Volume always uses all three dimensions. Cylinder = circle (πr²) extended by height. Sketch and label first.

atomic_skills.title: Calculate surface area of basic 3D shapes
atomic_skills.description: Rectangular prism: 2(lb + lh + bh). Cylinder: 2πr² + 2πrh. Use to find paint or wrapping required.

error_signatures.description: Counts only the visible faces
error_signatures.example: For a box, sums 3 faces instead of 6

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A closed prism has 6 faces (3 pairs). Cylinder has 2 circular ends + 1 curved side. Count carefully.

atomic_skills.title: Apply volume / surface area to real-world tasks
atomic_skills.description: Concrete foundation volume, water tank capacity, packaging surface area, paint coverage on irregular surfaces.

error_signatures.description: Uses volume when surface area is required (or vice versa)
error_signatures.example: Computes paint needed using volume of room instead of total wall area

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Paint covers SURFACES (area / surface area). Material filling a space (water, concrete) uses VOLUME.

levels.title: Maps, plans and physical world
levels.caps_section: Maps, plans and other representations of the physical world
levels.description: Use scale to convert between map / plan measurements and actual measurements. Read street and road maps. Interpret floor and elevation plans. Build and analyse models.

atomic_skills.title: Interpret scale and convert map ↔ actual measurements
atomic_skills.description: Read numerical scales (1:100, 1:50 000) and bar scales. Measure on map, multiply by scale factor, convert to real-world unit. Convert actual distance to map by dividing by scale factor.

error_signatures.description: Misreads 1:50 000 scale interpretation
error_signatures.example: Computes actual length as map × 50 000 cm and forgets to convert cm to km

error_signatures.description: Multiplies instead of dividing when going actual → map
error_signatures.example: For 5 m actual at 1:100, gives 500 cm map instead of 5 cm

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Map → actual: multiply (always bigger). Actual → map: divide (always smaller). Convert to readable unit at end.

atomic_skills.title: Choose or critique an appropriate scale
atomic_skills.description: Pick a scale that fits a drawing to available paper / screen. Critique whether a given scale produces a readable representation.

error_signatures.description: Picks a scale that doesn't fit on the page
error_signatures.example: Chooses 1:10 for a 30 m building on A4

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Divide actual longest dimension by available paper length. Round to common scale (1:50, 1:100, 1:500).

atomic_skills.title: Read maps and give/follow directions
atomic_skills.description: Identify roads, landmarks, names, compass directions using a key. Provide and follow step-by-step directions using street names.

error_signatures.description: Confuses north on map with top of page when rotated
error_signatures.example: Reports a feature 'north' because it's at the top of a rotated map

error_signatures.description: Mixes left/right from traveller's vs aerial perspective
error_signatures.example: Says 'turn left' when the route bends right from the traveller's heading

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Check the compass arrow before describing direction. Imagine walking the route, not looking down at it.

atomic_skills.title: Use distance charts, plan routes, estimate time and fuel
atomic_skills.description: Read a distance chart matrix. Compare routes. Use distance ÷ speed = time; consumption rate × distance = fuel litres × R/litre = fuel cost.

error_signatures.description: Forgets to sum stop-to-stop distances on multi-leg route
error_signatures.example: Reports just the longest leg instead of total

error_signatures.description: Uses consumption rate the wrong way (km/L vs L/100km)
error_signatures.example: Treats 8 L/100km as 8 km/L

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: List each leg; sum all. For consumption, read unit carefully (L/100km = fuel for 100km; km/L = km on 1L).

atomic_skills.title: Read floor and elevation plans
atomic_skills.description: Identify rooms, dimensions, doors, windows using the plan key. Recognise scale. Match features across multiple views (north/south/east/west elevations to the floor plan).

error_signatures.description: Confuses door symbol with window symbol
error_signatures.example: Counts windows on a plan including door swings

error_signatures.description: Cannot link elevation view to floor-plan side
error_signatures.example: Identifies a window on north elevation but cannot find it on the floor plan

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Check the key. Place the floor plan with compass arrow pointing north; each elevation is what you'd see standing outside, looking towards that side.

atomic_skills.title: Use plans to solve real tasks and critique designs
atomic_skills.description: Use plan + scale to determine carpet, paint, flooring, fencing. Comment on a proposed layout (kitchen/bathroom efficiency, flow, dimensions).

error_signatures.description: Uses plan measurements directly without applying scale
error_signatures.example: Orders carpet using the 10 cm dimension shown on the plan

error_signatures.description: Critiques aesthetic without grounding in function
error_signatures.example: Says layout is 'ugly' without identifying flow or use problems

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Apply scale first to get actual dimensions, then compute. Ground critique in function (e.g. 'bedroom door opens into kitchen workspace').

atomic_skills.title: Build models and compare packaging options
atomic_skills.description: Construct 3D models from a flat net or dimensions. Compare two models by volume (capacity) and surface area (material cost) to recommend one for a given purpose.

error_signatures.description: Folds a net in wrong order producing a broken shape
error_signatures.example: Folds a cube net with two faces overlapping

error_signatures.description: Compares only on volume, ignoring material/cost
error_signatures.example: Recommends the larger box without noting it uses 30% more cardboard

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Pre-fold lightly; check pairs of opposite faces. Always report both volume and surface area before recommending.

atomic_skills.title: Choose an appropriate scale for a model
atomic_skills.description: Pick a scale based on actual object size and available materials. Compute model dimensions from scale.

error_signatures.description: Chooses scale that makes model too small to handle
error_signatures.example: Picks 1:1000 for a 5m car, making it 5mm long

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Aim for handleable model size (~10-50 cm in longest dimension). Pick scale accordingly.

levels.title: Data handling
levels.caps_section: Data handling — Developing questions and collecting data; Classifying and organising; Measuring data; Representing data; Interpreting data
levels.description: The full data cycle: design and run a data collection, classify and organise, summarise with measures of central tendency and spread, represent in tables / charts, interpret and critique.

atomic_skills.title: Develop questions and choose a sample
atomic_skills.description: Write a survey question respondents can answer without ambiguity (avoid leading or double-barrelled). Pick a sample that reflects the population; recognise convenience samples introduce bias.

error_signatures.description: Asks a double-barrelled question
error_signatures.example: 'Do you eat fruit and vegetables daily?'

error_signatures.description: Surveys friends only and generalises
error_signatures.example: Surveys 5 friends and reports as 'students think...'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: One concept per question. Ask: are all subgroups represented? Convenience samples are easy but biased.

atomic_skills.title: Design, run and critique a questionnaire
atomic_skills.description: Construct a questionnaire of 5-10 well-formed questions. Administer to the sample. Critique a questionnaire for bias (leading wording, sample, missing options).

error_signatures.description: Asks open-text questions you can't analyse quantitatively
error_signatures.example: Asks 10 free-text questions that can't be tabulated

error_signatures.description: Only critiques wording, missing sample bias
error_signatures.example: Edits a question but ignores that the sample was only male

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use closed questions for things to count. Check three for bias: wording, sample, response options.

atomic_skills.title: Classify data types and complete frequency tables
atomic_skills.description: Distinguish categorical from numerical, discrete from continuous. Tally raw data; record counts in a frequency table; compute relative frequencies.

error_signatures.description: Calls a count-based variable continuous
error_signatures.example: Calls 'number of cars per family' continuous

error_signatures.description: Frequency totals don't match dataset size
error_signatures.example: Frequencies sum to 38 but dataset has 40

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Discrete = integer counts. Continuous = any value in a range. After tabulating, sum frequencies and confirm equals count.

atomic_skills.title: Group continuous data into intervals
atomic_skills.description: Choose appropriate interval width. Group raw data into intervals (0-10, 10-20, ...). Decide endpoint convention (≤ vs <).

error_signatures.description: Double-counts boundary values
error_signatures.example: Counts value 10 in both 0-10 and 10-20 intervals

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use a single convention: 0 ≤ x < 10 means 10 goes in the next interval.

atomic_skills.title: Calculate mean, median and mode
atomic_skills.description: Mean = sum ÷ count. Median = middle of sorted data (mean of two middle for even count). Mode = most frequent value.

error_signatures.description: Reports median without sorting first
error_signatures.example: For [3, 8, 5, 1, 9], picks 5 (middle of unsorted) by chance — fails when middle changes

error_signatures.description: Divides by wrong count for mean
error_signatures.example: Divides by number of categories instead of items

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Always sort first for median. Count items first; that's the divisor for mean.

atomic_skills.title: Calculate range, quartiles and choose the right average
atomic_skills.description: Range = max − min. Quartiles divide sorted data into 4 parts; IQR = Q3 − Q1. Decide which average best represents a dataset (mean for symmetric, median for outlier-prone, mode for categorical).

error_signatures.description: Confuses Q2 with mean
error_signatures.example: Reports Q2 as the dataset's mean

error_signatures.description: Picks mean for skewed data; reports misleading 'typical'
error_signatures.example: Reports mean salary R45k when 9 of 10 earn R20k and one earns R270k

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Q2 = median. Q1 / Q3 = medians of lower / upper halves. For skewed data with outliers, median is more representative.

atomic_skills.title: Read and construct bar, pie, line and histogram charts
atomic_skills.description: Identify values, compare categories, note trends. Choose the right chart for the data type (bars for category comparison, pies for parts-of-whole, lines for change over time, histograms for grouped continuous data).

error_signatures.description: Misreads pie chart percentage as count
error_signatures.example: Reports a 30% pie slice as '30 people'

error_signatures.description: Leaves gaps between histogram bars (confuses with bar chart)
error_signatures.example: Draws histogram of heights with spaces between bars

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Check chart legend and axis units. Histograms (continuous) touch; bar charts (categorical) have gaps.

atomic_skills.title: Construct scatter plots and box-and-whisker
atomic_skills.description: Scatter: relationship between two variables. Box-and-whisker: distribution summary (min, Q1, median, Q3, max).

error_signatures.description: Uses line graph for unordered categorical data
error_signatures.example: Draws line graph connecting 'Apple', 'Banana', 'Cherry'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Scatter for relationship between two numerical variables. Box-and-whisker needs the 5 summary values.

atomic_skills.title: Analyse trends and critique misleading graphs
atomic_skills.description: Identify increasing / decreasing / cyclic patterns. Use trends to predict future values cautiously. Spot truncated axes, distorted scales, cherry-picked time ranges, 3D effects that mislead.

error_signatures.description: Extrapolates a trend without considering plausibility
error_signatures.example: Predicts a population doubles every decade for 200 years based on a 10-year trend

error_signatures.description: Spots distortion but cannot explain the impact
error_signatures.example: Says 'the axis is wrong' without explaining how it overstates a small difference

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Trends project safely only a short distance beyond the data. Finish critique with: 'This makes [variable] look [bigger/smaller] than it is, because [reason].'

atomic_skills.title: Compare two datasets using central tendency and spread
atomic_skills.description: Use mean / median and IQR / range to compare two groups (e.g. boys vs girls in an exam). Make a justified statement.

error_signatures.description: Compares only means, ignoring spread
error_signatures.example: Says 'Group A is better' on mean alone when A has very high spread

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Report both a centre value AND a spread value before comparing.

levels.title: Probability
levels.caps_section: Probability — Expressions of probability; Prediction; Evaluating
levels.description: Express, calculate, combine and critique probability in real-world contexts: weather, games, risk assessments, medical tests.

atomic_skills.title: Identify outcomes and express probability
atomic_skills.description: List all possible outcomes of a single event (die, coin, card draw). Recognise the sample space. Express probability as fraction, decimal, or percentage; convert between forms.

error_signatures.description: Misses an outcome
error_signatures.example: Lists die outcomes as {1,2,3,4,5}, missing 6

error_signatures.description: Treats 0,25 and 25 as same probability value
error_signatures.example: Reports probability as 25 when it should be 0,25 or 25%

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Be systematic — list in order and count. Probability is always between 0 and 1 (or 0% and 100%).

atomic_skills.title: Place probabilities on the 0-1 scale
atomic_skills.description: Anchor: 0 = impossible, 0,5 = even chance, 1 = certain. Place real-world probabilities (rain forecast, exam pass rate) on the scale and use matching language (likely/unlikely/very likely).

error_signatures.description: Uses language inconsistent with numeric value
error_signatures.example: Calls 80% chance of rain 'unlikely'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Match language to value. > 0,5 = more likely than not. Close to 1 = very likely. Close to 0 = very unlikely.

atomic_skills.title: Calculate theoretical and experimental probability
atomic_skills.description: Theoretical: P(event) = favourable outcomes ÷ total outcomes (assumes equally likely). Experimental: P(event) ≈ times event occurred ÷ total trials.

error_signatures.description: Swaps numerator and denominator
error_signatures.example: For rolling a 4, gives 6/1 instead of 1/6

error_signatures.description: Reports raw count instead of ratio
error_signatures.example: Reports 'heads occurred 53 times' as probability instead of 53/100

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Numerator = favourable ways; denominator = total possible. Probability is always a ratio.

atomic_skills.title: Compare theoretical and experimental probability
atomic_skills.description: Compute both for the same scenario. Explain why they may differ in small samples and why they converge with more trials.

error_signatures.description: Claims result is 'wrong' if experimental and theoretical differ
error_signatures.example: Says 'experiment is broken' when 47 heads in 100 flips doesn't match 50/50

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Small samples can deviate. Larger samples (1000+) converge to theoretical probability.

atomic_skills.title: Use tables / trees to calculate combined probabilities
atomic_skills.description: For two events, construct a two-way table or tree diagram to enumerate combined outcomes. Calculate P(combined) = favourable combined ÷ total combined. Interpret 'and' (multiply for independent) and 'or' (add for mutually exclusive).

error_signatures.description: Misses branches on a tree diagram
error_signatures.example: For two coin flips, lists HH, HT, TT but omits TH

error_signatures.description: Treats 'and' as 'or' (adds when should multiply)
error_signatures.example: For P(heads AND a 6), adds P(H) + P(6) instead of multiplying

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Each event 1 branch splits into all event 2 branches. Independent + 'and' = multiply. Mutually exclusive + 'or' = add.

atomic_skills.title: Critique claims and analyse fairness / risk
atomic_skills.description: Critique claims in media ('lottery numbers, weather predictions'). Calculate expected outcomes (probability × payoff) to determine if a game is fair. Analyse insurance / risk-band tables to explain pricing differences.

error_signatures.description: Accepts a misconception about independence
error_signatures.example: Agrees 'taking same lottery numbers improves chances' without noting independence

error_signatures.description: Calls a game fair without checking expected value
error_signatures.example: Says R10 game with R30 prize on 1/4 chance is fair (expected R7,50 < R10 cost makes it unfair)

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Each draw is independent — past results don't change future probabilities. Fair game: expected payout = entry cost.
